pr_title: Use Enter instead of F2 as an editor renaming shortcut on macOS (3.x)
pr_body:
`3.x` version of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/54924.

Tested locally by using `KEY_ENTER` as a shortcut in the Scene tree dock and FileSystem dock, it works as expected. The same shortcut override can't be used in the project manager due to a conflict though.

This closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/54923.

issue_context.title: Wrong key to rename file/folder in MacOS
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

3.4.stable

### System information

MacBook Pro (16-inch, 2019), Monterey, GLES3

### Issue description

`F2` key is used to rename files in editor in MacOS version. 
`return` should be used as it is default in MacOS for renaming.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/57115583/141511076-0408c293-afe4-447a-ab3e-74a547107b32.png)


### Steps to reproduce

Open Godot editor MacOS version and try to rename file or folder

### Minimal reproduction project

_No response_

review_comments: Should there be a different shortcut to edit the project on macOS maybe? What would be idiomatic there? Cmd+E? CC @godotengine/macos

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/47894 already added <kbd>Ctrl + E</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd + E</kbd> to edit a project. On the other hand, I think many people expect <kbd>Enter</kbd> to edit a project as it's more discoverable.
